A tip truck is a truck used for transporting loose materials (such as sand, gravel or dirt) for construction. A typical tip truck is equipped with an open-box bed, which is hinged at the rear and equipped with hydraulic pistons to lift the front, allowing the materials in the bed to be deposited (dumped) on the ground behind the truck at the site of delivery.

Agent: Absolutely! The hydraulic pistons in a tip truck are what make it possible to lift the front end of the bed and dump the cargo. Here is a step-by-step overview of how they work:

1. The driver activates the hydraulic system by operating a control lever in the cab of the truck.

2. This control lever activates a pump which sends hydraulic fluid to the hydraulic pistons.

3. The hydraulic pistons are typically located underneath the bed and are connected to the frame of the truck.

4. When hydraulic fluid is pumped into the pistons, it causes them to extend, which in turn lifts the front end of the bed upwards.

5. As the bed tilts, gravity causes the cargo to slide out of the back and onto the ground.

6. Once the cargo has been dumped, the driver can release the control lever, which allows the hydraulic fluid to flow out of the pistons, causing the bed to lower back into its original position.

The hydraulic pistons are typically made of stainless steel or another durable material, and they are designed to withstand a great deal of force as they lift and lower the heavy weight of the cargo. The hydraulic system allows for precise control over the speed and angle of the bed tilt, which helps to ensure accurate and safe dumping of the cargo. Overall, the hydraulic pistons are a critical component of the tip truck, enabling it to transport large quantities of loose materials quickly and efficiently.

Agent: Certainly! Automatic tarps are a common feature in many modern tip trucks, especially those used for transporting loose materials such as sand, gravel, or dirt. Here's how they work:

1. The automatic tarp system consists of an electric motor or hydraulic pump and a roll of heavy-duty tarp material that is stored in a housing mounted to the truck bed.

2. When the driver is ready to cover the load, he or she activates the tarp system using a control switch located in the cab of the truck.

3. The electric motor or hydraulic pump then unwinds the tarp from the housing and extends it over the length of the bed.

4. The tarp material is pulled tight over the bed using a series of rollers or springs, ensuring that the load is securely covered and preventing loose materials from flying out during transport.

5. Once the load is covered, the driver can deactivate the tarp system, causing the tarp to retract back into its housing and allowing the truck to be driven.

Automatic tarp systems offer several important benefits for tip truck operators. First and foremost, they improve safety by containing the load and preventing loose materials from being blown out of the truck bed during transport. This can significantly reduce the risk of accidents and injuries caused by materials flying into the road, hitting other vehicles, or striking pedestrians.

In addition to improving safety, automatic tarps can also save time and money by reducing the amount of cleanup required after transport. With the load securely covered, there is less risk of materials spilling onto the road or other surfaces, which means that cleanup crews can get to work more quickly and efficiently. Overall, automatic tarps are an important feature that can help ensure safe and efficient operation of a tip truck.

Fashion can also be used to convey themes in literature. For example, in Margaret Atwood's The Handmaid's Tale, the red robes worn by the Handmaids represent their subjugation and the loss of their individual identities. Similarly, in Charlotte Bronte's Jane Eyre, the simple and modest clothing of the protagonist reflects her own values of morality and decency.

The portrayal of fashion in literature has evolved over time, reflecting cultural shifts and trends. In Victorian literature, clothing played a significant role in defining social class, and authors often described in detail the elaborate dresses and accessories of the upper classes. In contrast, modern literature tends to focus more on individual expression and personal style, with less emphasis on traditional markers of socioeconomic status.

The impact of modern technologies and social media on the relationship between fashion and literature cannot be ignored. The rise of fashion blogging and Instagram influencers has created a new platform for fashion to be showcased and discussed, blurring the lines between fashion and literature. Many modern writers incorporate fashion into their work in new and innovative ways, such as using fashion as a tool for exploring issues of identity and representation.

In conclusion, the interplay between fashion and literature is complex and multifaceted. Through the use of clothing and accessories, authors can convey character traits, societal trends, and themes, while fashion trends and cultural shifts have influenced the portrayal of fashion in literature. As modern technologies and social media continue to reshape the way we see and communicate fashion, it will be interesting to see how literature responds and adapts to these changes.

Unlike a few industry competitors, one automaker at MWC believes that partnering will be critical for autonomous vehicle rollouts. “We know [about the things] we do very well, but we can’t do things alone. We have started partnerships not only with core tech companies, but others in adjacent services,” said Ogi Redzic, Renault-Nissan Alliance senior vice president, connected vehicles and mobility services, at a MWC autonomous vehicle panel.
Redzic said his company is working with companies as diverse as Microsoft for cloud vehicle security, a large transit company and Japanese gaming companies to introduce driving services that interact with people and to add new development capabilities.
Redzic said his company hopes to bring on 300 additional experts in the autonomous vehicle industry. “There is a skills gap, not just automotive, but transformational,” he said.
In terms of new markets, Redzic believes urban mobility, with electric connected and autonomous cars as a centerpiece, will be a solid segment for his company. “In order for us to deploy [autonomous vehicles] in the 200 countries we sell cars, costs of hardware have to come down. In particular LiDAR. High-definition maps need to be available,” he said.
Renalut-Nissan said it plans to roll out at least 10 car models, by 2020, with some sort of autonomous driving capability. The Nissan Serena, a minivan sold in Japan, has single-lane autonomous drive capability through the company’s ProPilot technology.

“High-quality connectivity is the base for autonomous vehicles. The next step for autonomous vehicles is 5G vehicle-to-vehicle and infrastructure connectivity,” said Nikolai Reimer, Volkswagen head of mobile online services and connectivity.
Reimer said that Volkswagen, three years ago, bought a former Blackberry team to design connectivity modules. “The connectivity units, developed in house with module and microchip suppliers, were deployed early to influence chip design. Autonomous driving without this connectivity is not possible,” he said.
While many automakers save their announcements for the larger auto shows, particular in Geneva, MWC saw a few. Ford, which has exhibited at MWC for the past five years, rolled out its Autolivery that uses an electric self-driving van and drones to deliver packages in cities.
Drones are launched, within a few meters of final delivery, to take packages to multistory buildings and areas where a vehicle can’t operate.
Peugeot showed off its Instinct concept car, which can operate in a self-driving mode. The car incorporates an onboard Internet of Things (IoT) platform with Samsung’s Artik Cloud service. This allows it to collect data from other connected devices and adjust settings to include audio, lighting, seat, interface settings and others.
Qualcomm and TomTom are partnering to create high-definition maps for autonomous cars. Qualcomm’s Drive Data Platform and TomTom’s HD Map tool will be used in the collaboration, the companies say. To gather data, the companies plan to use crowdsourcing and machine learning.

User: French car major Renault made its biggest splash in India yet unveiling its small car Kwid on Wednesday. It will be launched ahead of the festive season this year and priced at Rs. 3-4 lakh.
The car will compete with India's largest selling car for over a decade-- Maruti Alto, and Hyundai Eon. Powered by a 800cc petrol engine and developed as part of Renault Nissan alliance's new frugal CMF-A (common module family-affordable) platform, the French firm expects Kwid will go a long way in helping it achieve not only its target marketshare of 5% but also in breaking even in India in the medium term.
"After the Duster, Kwid will be our next global car," said Carlos Ghosn, CEO, Renault Nissan. "I expect it to be a gamechanger in India. This is the only car that is being launched with an over-97% local content. India is a very tough market and we have learnt a lot of lessons here. The car is a result of five years of learning. If it succeeds with good numbers here, we are sure it will be a success in any other market that we launch it globally."
The platform will be used for many more cars including Nissan's sister brand Datsun's upcoming Redi Go small car, slated to be launched in India next year. Renault claims Kwid will offer best in class fuel economy, interior space and boot space.
"India is not a very easy market for newcomers and with the Kwid we are paying tribute to whatever we have learnt here," Ghosn added. "We cannot escape from the fact that in the next 5 years the Indian market holds a big potential. India and China are the only two markets with a certain size that can grow at over 6% annually. We believe India can be world's fourth largest car market behind China, US and Japan."
Renault said it has spent close to Rs. 2,000 crore towards development of the model but added that the investment was 50% less than what it would entail in most cases. Renault shares it factory at Oragadam on the outskirts of Chennai with Nissan that means sharing fixed costs and helps contain investments. Ghosn, however, added there would be no cross-badging of cars between the two companies anymore.
"Nissan will use the same platform, engine transmission etcetra but it will be a different design and appeal to different set of customers," Ghosn added.
How does the Kwid fit into Renault Nissan alliance's new frugal CMF-A platform and what other cars will be built using this platform?

The French car giant claims the Kwid will offer the best in class fuel economy, interior space and boot space, and is a result of five years of learning in India.
